_about.dataset: STRUM — dyadic multimodal neuroergonomics recordings (SCCN, UC San Diego)
_about.purpose: Per-session / per-participant inventory of the STRUM BIDS dataset: delivered block structure, modality coverage, EEG montage and channel counts.

terms.session: One dyad's visit to the lab, BIDS `ses-NN`, cross-referenced to the original study-session number (`study`). Both participants of a dyad share one session and one event timeline.
terms.recording: One continuous XDF recording of a session (BIDS `run-N` entity). A second recording is a restart or a continuation of the same experimental sequence, NOT an experimental repeat — see ADR-0004. `recording_model` is one of: single, restart (the sequence was rerun), continuation (the block sequence carries on into the next recording).
terms.block: An experimental block. The design delivers 5 blocks, indexed 0–4, with roughly 6, 4, 6, 5 and 4 missions (25 missions total).
terms.mission: One task episode inside a block, either individual or cooperative. `missions` counts the missions observed per block; 0 means the block began but delivered no mission.
terms.lull: An inter-block rest period. A complete session has 4 inter-block lulls.
terms.coverage: 1 = the modality is present for that participant in the released BIDS tree, 0 = absent in the source (never fabricated). `eye` = eye_gaze OR eye_scene, the streams that carry usable gaze behaviour; `eye_any` also counts hotspot-only participants and is therefore looser.
terms.station: Which of the two seats/hosts the participant used: Delta or Echo. Each station has its own amplifier, cap, eye-tracker, force plate and controller.
terms.montage: EEG montage variant. `scalp_eeg` is the number of scalp EEG channels (207 for the full 256-ch cap, 162 for the one early small-cap dyad); `total_ch` is every signal channel written for that participant.
terms.sync: LSL clock quality for the session, from the ClockOffset sweep (scripts/analyze_sync.py). `interbrain_*` is the jitter between the dyad's TWO EEG amplifiers — they sit on different hosts, so this is the alignment a hyperscanning analysis inherits, and it is the number to filter on. `same_host_us` covers the recorder-local streams (mocap, one amp, one plate). All values are residual SD of a global linear fit, a conservative upper bound. One sample at 512 Hz is 1.95 ms, for reference.
terms.av: Audio/video status. `restricted` = identifiable media exist but live in `sourcedata/av/`, outside the released subject tree; `audio-only` = no video in the source; `none` = neither.

notes: Blocks are 5 (0–4), not 3: ADR-0004's original 3-block claim was corrected.
Both members of a dyad share one byte-identical event timeline.
23 participants have no eye-tracking in the source.
Audio/video are restricted and never released as subject data.
Force is 57/66: one seat's plate was absent and 8 more recorded zero samples (per-session hardware dropouts, root-caused against the source XDF and skipped by the exporter) — see dataset-review.md.
